national_raw_news.title: Several Indian athletes begin medal hunt today at 20th Asian Games 2026 6 mins ago 5
national_raw_news.content: The 20th Asian Games 2026 will see several Indian athletes begin their medal hunt across multiple disciplines today. Indian shooters Elavenil Valarivan, Sonam Maskar and Vidarsa Vinod will aim for podium finishes in the women’s 10m air rifle event. The trio will compete for both individual and team medals. The Indian women’s hockey team will also begin its campaign today, facing Uzbekistan in its opening group-stage match. The men’s hockey team will take on Indonesia in their first match of the tournament. In today’s cricket event, the Indian women’s team will face Bangladesh in the semifinal. The knockout match will start at 10:30 AM IST at the Aichi Prefectural Korogi Sports Park in Nisshin, Japan. The Indian teqball player Quimcy Dsouza missed out on a women’s singles bronze medal after suffering a 2-0 defeat to home favourite Yuina Sakamoto in a closely contested match. Sakomoto prevailed 12-11, 12-11 in a match that saw both games go down to the wire, leaving Dsouza to rue several missed opportunities. The Indian had chances to take control of the contest, holding set point in the opening game before Sakamoto fought back. Dsouza also established a lead in the second game and even saved a match point with a winning serve, but was unable to close out the contest as Sakamoto capitalised on crucial errors at the decisive moments. However, Dsouza will have another opportunity to claim a medal as she is set to compete in the mixed doubles bronze medal match alongside Mohamed Anas Beg.

national_raw_news.title: BJP Punjab’s ‘Nasha Mukt Punjab Yatras’ got remarkable response from people of state 30 mins ago 15
national_raw_news.content: Bharatiya Janata Party(BJP) Punjab’s “Nasha Mukt Punjab Yatras”, which the party’s National President, Nitin Nabin, launched from the border district of Pathankot on September 18th, is getting a remarkable response from the people of the state. Yesterday, Delhi Chief Minister Rekha Gupta, while launching the second out of four phases of the Yatras from Fatehgarh Sahib, termed it a movement of a new beginning in Punjab. She said ‘Nasha Mukt Punjab Yatra’ is not merely a political programme but a call for collective action to free Punjab from drugs, crime and fear. This 13-day long ‘Nasha Mukt Punjab Yatra ’, which has started with a tagline of – ‘Bhajpa Da Naara – Nasha Mukana Saara’ is focusing on three major challenges presently confronting Punjab. These are the growing drug menace, deteriorating law and order, and corruption at every level of governance. The Yatra will cover 4000 kilometres in the state to mobilise people from across all 117 Assembly constituencies to turn the fight against drugs into a mass public movement. The third yatra will be launched today by Union Minister of State for Law and Justice, Arjun Ram Meghwal, from Fazilka’s Sadiqi border, and tomorrow, the fourth phase will be flagged off by Union Agriculture Minister, Shivraj Singh Chouhan, and Haryana Chief Minister, Nayab Singh Saini, from Talwandi Sabo in Bathinda. The ‘Nasha Mukt Punjab Yatra’ will conclude on September 30th at Jalandhar, in which Union Home Minister Amit Shah is scheduled to participate.
